rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Vegetation conservation protects natural plant cover through in-situ strategies (protected areas, community forests, sacred groves) and ex-situ strategies (botanical gardens, seed banks, tissue culture, herbaria). Nepal's community-forestry program (22,000+ groups managing ~36% of forest land) is one of the world's most successful.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
In-situ: protected areas + community forests + sacred groves (in natural habitat)
Ex-situ: botanical gardens + seed banks + tissue culture + herbaria (outside habitat)
Threats: jhum + grazing + firewood + logging + climate change + pollution

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: In-situ conservation protects vegetation IN its natural habitat; ex-situ conserves plant material OUTSIDE (botanical gardens, seed banks).  ·  Community forests (in-situ) give local communities rights and responsibility; they differ from government-managed national parks.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a clear in-situ vs ex-situ conservation distinction with Nepali examples.  ·  Community forestry (~36% of forest land) is a key Nepali success story.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: In-situ: Chitwan, Sagarmatha, Annapurna, Kanchenjunga national parks; community forests; sacred groves (deval-ghari).  ·  Ex-situ: Nepal National Herbarium, seed banks, botanical gardens, tissue-culture labs.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Jhum (shifting/slash-and-burn) agriculture is a major cause of hill deforestation; it is different from permanent agriculture.  ·  A sacred grove (deval-ghari) is a traditionally protected forest patch; it is a form of in-situ conservation.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Differentiate in-situ vs ex-situ  ·  Explain community forestry

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: In-situ = IN habitat; Ex-situ = EX (outside) habitat.  ·  Community forestry = ~36% of Nepal's forest land.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Differentiate in-situ from ex-situ vegetation conservation.  ·  Explain the role of community forestry in Nepal.

rows.text: In-situ vs ex-situ conservation  ·  Community forestry  ·  Sacred groves  ·  Jhum agriculture

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Vegetation conservation: in-situ + ex-situ strategies.  ·  In-situ: protected areas, community forests, sacred groves.  ·  Ex-situ: botanical gardens, seed banks, tissue culture, herbaria.  ·  Nepal: community forestry (~36% of forest land) is a global success story.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: ~64% of Nepal's area is under forest; ~35% is evergreen.  ·  Community forest groups (22,000+) manage ~36% of Nepal's forest land — one of the most successful community-forestry programs in the world.

rows.text: Threats: jhum agriculture, over-grazing, firewood collection, illegal logging, climate change.  ·  Importance: oxygen, climate regulation, soil conservation, water, biodiversity, food, medicine, culture.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Vegetation conservation: protecting and managing natural plant cover; includes in-situ and ex-situ strategies.  ·  In-situ conservation: protecting vegetation in its natural location — protected areas (national parks, conservation areas, wildlife reserves), community forests, sacred groves.  ·  Ex-situ conservation: conserving plant material outside the natural habitat — botanical gardens, seed banks, tissue culture, herbaria.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Vegetation threats  ·  Importance of vegetation  ·  Natural environment-vegetation

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Water cycle and soil conservation  ·  Importance: oxygen + climate + soil + water + biodiversity + food + medicine + culture  ·  Threats: jhum, grazing, firewood, logging, climate change, pollution.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Importance: oxygen, climate, soil, water, biodiversity, food, medicine, culture.  ·  Natural environment-vegetation: forests regulate the water cycle and prevent erosion.  ·  Deforestation disrupts the water cycle and causes erosion, landslides, and climate change — not just loss of trees.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Ex-situ (seed banks, tissue culture) is a back-up; it cannot fully replace in-situ conservation of whole ecosystems.  ·  Natural environment-vegetation: forests regulate the water cycle, prevent erosion, and stabilise the climate.  ·  Jhum (shifting) agriculture is a major cause of hill deforestation — a frequent exam point.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: List the threats to vegetation (5+).  ·  Explain the importance of vegetation to the natural environment (water cycle, soil, climate, biodiversity).  ·  Sacred groves (deval-ghari) are a traditional in-situ conservation form.
